findings.title: The covenant returns as binding means
findings.claim: The pronoun بِهِۦ returns the covenant as the means and accompaniment of the binding act.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the bi prefix at 5:7:8:1 and pronoun at 5:7:8:2. Trigger: its antecedent mīthāq at 5:7:5:2 and the relational verb at 5:7:7:1. Contact: the pronoun links the covenant back into the verb as instrument. Result: the covenant remains active in the binding action rather than remaining a detached noun.
findings.reader_payoff: The covenant is perceived as an operative bond within the sentence, not merely a promise remembered from the past.
findings.containment: This is a local instrumental relation; it does not claim that every occurrence of bi or every covenant is instrumental.

epistemic.reason: Resolved focus alignment and trusted local word-analysis evidence directly support the pronoun's attachment and function.

findings.title: The covenant is tied to a spoken moment
findings.claim: إِذْ locates the covenant in the moment when the addressees declared their response.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the temporal particle at 5:7:9:1. Trigger: the quoted speech introduced by the verb at 5:7:10:1 and its suffix at 5:7:10:2. Contact: the particle turns from the described covenant to the time of saying. Result: the quotation becomes the remembered content of a specific covenant scene.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees a precise remembered moment rather than vague historical background behind the covenant.
findings.containment: The particle fixes the local temporal hinge; it does not independently specify every detail of the historical setting.

epistemic.reason: Trusted word-analysis evidence and resolved focus alignment support the temporal attachment.

findings.title: The quoted words are covenant evidence
findings.claim: قُلْتُمْ makes the addressees completed speakers whose own utterance functions as evidence within the covenant command.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the completed plural speech verb at 5:7:10:1 and suffix at 5:7:10:2. Trigger: the formula at 5:7:11:1, 5:7:11:2, 5:7:12:1, 5:7:12:2, and 5:7:12:3. Contact: the speech verb frames the quoted response as their prior declaration. Result: the covenant is voiced through the addressees' declared posture, not merely described by the narrator.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears the covenant as something the addressed community itself once said and thereby entered into.
findings.containment: The performative force is limited to this quoted covenant declaration; it does not make every utterance a covenant-making act.

epistemic.reason: Trusted local word-analysis evidence supports the completed speech form and its quotation frame.

findings.title: Hearing is covenant reception
findings.claim: سَمِعْنَا presents hearing as completed reception and assent within the covenant frame, not sound perception alone.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the first-person plural perfect at 5:7:11:1 and suffix at 5:7:11:2. Trigger: its open object is supplied by the covenant frame and the following obedience at 5:7:12:2 and 5:7:12:3. Contact: hearing is paired with an enacted response. Result: the declaration includes understanding and acceptance of what was received.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the first half of the formula as a response that takes in a command, rather than as a report about ears.
findings.containment: The receptive extension stays within this covenant response; the form does not erase the ordinary sense of hearing.

epistemic.reason: Trusted word-analysis evidence and the resolved focus alignment support the local receptive attachment.

findings.title: Hearing and obedience are paired
findings.claim: The وَ between سَمِعْنَا and أَطَعْنَا coordinates hearing and obedience as two parts of the same response.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the conjunction at 5:7:12:1. Trigger: the two completed response verbs at 5:7:11:1 and 5:7:12:2. Contact: the conjunction places the verbs side by side under the quotation. Result: reception and compliance arrive as a paired covenant declaration.
findings.reader_payoff: The response becomes audible as a joined formula whose two halves must be held together.
findings.containment: The coordination does not claim that the two verbs are identical; it preserves their distinct contributions within one response.

epistemic.reason: Trusted local evidence directly supports the conjunction's coordinating function.

findings.title: Obedience completes the response
findings.claim: أَطَعْنَا completes the quoted response by presenting compliance as willing obedience.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the first-person plural Form IV perfect at 5:7:12:2 and suffix at 5:7:12:3. Trigger: the received command represented by سَمِعْنَا at 5:7:11:1 and 5:7:11:2. Contact: the second verb moves reception into declared action. Result: the covenant formula includes entered compliance rather than hearing alone.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader notices the movement from receiving a command to bringing oneself into its obedience.
findings.containment: The open object stays within the covenant frame; this does not specify an unlisted command or turn the form into a universal account of obedience.

epistemic.reason: Trusted word-analysis evidence supports the form, first-person subject, and response relation.

findings.title: The quotation opens a second command
findings.claim: The وَ after the quoted response links remembered speech to a new present imperative.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the conjunction at 5:7:13:1. Trigger: the completed quote ending at 5:7:12:3 and the imperative beginning at 5:7:13:2 and 5:7:13:3. Contact: the connector carries the sentence across the quotation boundary. Result: remembered declaration leads directly into present vigilance.
findings.reader_payoff: The ayah's movement continues beyond recalling what was said and reaches conduct demanded now.
findings.containment: The conjunction links these local clauses; it does not by itself establish a wider sequence beyond the supplied ayah.

epistemic.reason: Trusted local word-analysis evidence supports the post-quote connective relation.

findings.title: Guarding becomes present conduct
findings.claim: ٱتَّقُوا۟ makes self-guarding the present conduct demanded after the remembered declaration.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the plural Form VIII imperative at 5:7:13:2 and suffix at 5:7:13:3. Trigger: the second-imperative link at 5:7:13:1 and the preceding quoted response. Contact: the reflexive protective form turns covenant memory toward the addressees' own conduct. Result: vigilance is active self-guarding, not merely inward fear.
findings.reader_payoff: The warning is perceived as a practical protective posture that must continue after the words have been spoken.
findings.containment: The reading stays with active self-guarding in relation to this command; it does not broaden into every possible meaning of taqwa.

epistemic.reason: Trusted word-analysis evidence supports the Form VIII imperative and its local pivot from speech to conduct.

findings.title: The repeated divine name is the guarding object
findings.claim: The second occurrence of Allah is the direct object of the guarding command, making the vigilance specifically God-directed.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the accusative divine name at 5:7:14:1. Trigger: the imperative ٱتَّقُوا۟ at 5:7:13:2 and its suffix at 5:7:13:3. Contact: the accusative attachment identifies what the addressees are to guard in relation to. Result: the repeated name shifts from favor source to command object before the final knowledge clause.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the warning has a named divine orientation rather than functioning as generic caution.
findings.containment: The grammatical object role is local; it does not claim that the name itself is something to protect or that the two occurrences have identical roles.

epistemic.reason: Trusted evidence supports the object relation, while the finding preserves the change in role between repeated name occurrences.

findings.title: The closing knowledge is asserted
findings.claim: إِنَّ opens the final clause as an emphatic assertion that grounds the preceding commands in standing divine knowledge.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the emphatic particle at 5:7:15:1. Trigger: the clause headed by Allah at 5:7:16:1 and completed by the knowledge predicate. Contact: the particle marks the final statement as an asserted ground for the preceding exhortation. Result: the commands close upon an explicit knowledge claim.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final sentence as the stated ground of accountability, not as an unstated assumption.
findings.containment: The finding concerns the clause's emphatic force and does not assign an additional unstated proposition to the particle.

epistemic.reason: Trusted local word-analysis evidence directly supports the emphatic close.

findings.title: The opening command continues the discourse
findings.claim: The initial وَ makes the remembrance command a continuation of the preceding discourse.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the opening conjunction at 5:7:1:1. Trigger: the direct imperative at 5:7:1:2 and its suffix at 5:7:1:3. Contact: coordination carries the command into the prior sequence. Result: the ayah opens as chained accountability rather than an isolated maxim.
findings.reader_payoff: The first command arrives with the pressure of what has already been established around the addressed community.
findings.containment: This finding records continuation as supplied by the conjunction; it does not reconstruct any unsupplied preceding argument.

epistemic.reason: Trusted word-analysis evidence supports the connective opening and its local attachment.

findings.title: The named referent becomes the knowing subject
findings.claim: The second Allah occurrence is the accusative subject of إِنَّ and thus the subject of the final knowledge predicate.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the repeated divine name at 5:7:16:1. Trigger: إِنَّ at 5:7:15:1 and عَلِيمٌ at 5:7:17:1. Contact: the repeated name resets the clause with a new grammatical role. Result: the named referent is presented as the knower of the closing interior domain.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can follow the name's local movement from source of favor, through object of vigilance, to subject of knowledge.
findings.containment: The role sequence is a local grammatical observation; it does not rank the three name occurrences or claim they are interchangeable.

epistemic.reason: Trusted word-analysis evidence supports the ism-inna role and its predicate relation.

findings.title: Knowledge is presented as stable
findings.claim: عَلِيمٌ presents divine knowing as a stable intensive predicate directed toward the interior domain.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the faʿīl-form predicate at 5:7:17:1. Trigger: the following bi prefix at 5:7:18:1 and construct head at 5:7:18:2. Contact: the predicate's form and its attached domain make knowing a standing attribute reaching inward. Result: the close asserts durable knowledge rather than a passing act of noticing.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader perceives the final knowledge claim as a settled quality that reaches the hidden interior named next.
findings.containment: The stable-knowledge reading is limited to the supplied predicate form and local domain; it does not add a separate theory of divine attributes.

epistemic.reason: Trusted word-analysis evidence supports the predicate form and its local attachment.

findings.title: The preposition fastens knowledge to its domain
findings.claim: بِ binds the knowledge predicate directly to the interior phrase that follows.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the preposition at 5:7:18:1. Trigger: عَلِيمٌ at 5:7:17:1 and ذَاتِ at 5:7:18:2. Contact: the preposition links the predicate to its governed domain. Result: divine knowledge is grammatically fastened to what belongs to the chests, rather than left abstract.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees exactly where the final assertion lands: knowledge reaches the interior domain named at the end.
findings.containment: The claim concerns this prepositional attachment and does not generalize the full range of bi constructions.

epistemic.reason: Trusted local evidence directly supports the predicate-to-domain attachment.

findings.title: The interior phrase expresses belonging
findings.claim: ذَاتِ makes the object of knowledge what belongs intrinsically to the chests, not merely something located inside them.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the construct head at 5:7:18:2. Trigger: bi at 5:7:18:1 and the definite article at 5:7:19:1 with genitive plural at 5:7:19:2. Contact: the construct relation makes ذَاتِ govern the final domain while remaining governed by bi. Result: the phrase reaches inward belonging and essence.
findings.reader_payoff: The closing domain becomes the interior that belongs to the chests themselves, rather than a container filled with unrelated contents.
findings.containment: The finding stays with the supplied construct relation and does not claim that every use of ذَاتِ has this same force.

epistemic.reason: Trusted word-analysis evidence supports the construct-head and governed-domain relation.

findings.title: The ayah ends at the concealed interior domain
findings.claim: The definite plural الصُّدُورِ names the known collective chest domain and leaves the ayah on the concealed interior reached by divine knowledge.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the definite article at 5:7:19:1 and genitive plural at 5:7:19:2. Trigger: ذَاتِ at 5:7:18:2 and the final position of the noun. Contact: the final construct complement supplies the concrete interior domain of عَلِيمٌ. Result: the sentence closes on what lies within the chests rather than on the outward declaration.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah's final pressure move from spoken obedience to the hidden interior that God knows.
findings.containment: The lexical field supports chest, breast, source/front, and concealed inner seat here; no unstated external context is added.

epistemic.reason: Trusted local evidence supports the definite plural, construct complement, and final-domain effect.

findings.title: Remembrance is commanded as an active act
findings.claim: ٱذْكُرُوا۟ makes remembrance a direct present communal act that gathers favor and covenant under one command.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the Form I plural imperative at 5:7:1:2 and its 2MP suffix at 5:7:1:3. Trigger: the favor at 5:7:2:1 and the covenant conjunction at 5:7:5:1 with noun and suffix at 5:7:5:2 and 5:7:5:3. Contact: the imperative governs both the favor and the covenant. Result: remembrance is active recovery of both gift and binding obligation, with the supplied variant pressure kept subordinate to the local form.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears remembering as something the community is to do now, not as a passive mental reference to the past.
findings.containment: The local Form I imperative remains primary; variant evidence intensifies the act without replacing the supplied surface.

epistemic.reason: Trusted evidence supports the imperative and its paired objects; the qualification preserves the local form against overreading variant pressure.

findings.title: A specific favor comes before the bond
findings.claim: نِعْمَةَ is the singular first object of remembrance, so the covenantal demand is introduced through a specific conferred favor.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the singular accusative noun at 5:7:2:1. Trigger: its construct relation to Allah at 5:7:3:1 and coordination with the covenant conjunction at 5:7:5:1, noun at 5:7:5:2, and suffix at 5:7:5:3. Contact: the first object is named before the second while both remain governed by the imperative. Result: grace and obligation are joined in order without being collapsed.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the remembered duty arrives through a named favor before the sentence turns to the binding covenant.
findings.containment: The ordering is local and does not make favor the only content of the ayah or erase the separately coordinated covenant.

epistemic.reason: Trusted word-analysis evidence supports the first-object and construct relations, with the coordination boundary kept explicit.

findings.title: The named divine referent sources the favor
findings.claim: The first Allah occurrence grammatically makes the named divine referent the source and owner of the favor.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the genitive proper name at 5:7:3:1. Trigger: the construct noun نِعْمَةَ at 5:7:2:1. Contact: the genitive relation fixes whose favor is being recalled. Result: the first divine-name role is source of the remembered gift.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the gift as sourced under the named authority before that name returns in later grammatical roles.
findings.containment: The local construct establishes source and possession; derivational associations with the name remain outside this finding.

epistemic.reason: Trusted evidence supports the genitive source role while keeping broader derivational associations qualified.

findings.title: The favor is placed upon the addressees
findings.claim: عَلَيْكُمْ marks the plural addressees as the recipients upon whom the divine favor is directed.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the preposition at 5:7:4:1 and 2MP suffix at 5:7:4:2. Trigger: the favor at 5:7:2:1 and its genitive source at 5:7:3:1. Contact: the prepositional phrase attaches the favor to its addressed recipients. Result: the sentence moves from named source to the community that receives the favor.
findings.reader_payoff: The audience is made present as the community carrying the favor, not as a detached observer of someone else's gift.
findings.containment: The finding follows the local favor attachment; it does not settle every possible attachment of عَلَيْكُمْ or import an external historical account.

epistemic.reason: Trusted candidate evidence and resolved alignment support the source-to-recipient relation, with local attachment kept explicit.

findings.title: Covenant is the second object of remembrance
findings.claim: The وَ before مِيثَاقَهُ coordinates the covenant as a second object of the same recall command.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the conjunction at 5:7:5:1. Trigger: the covenant noun at 5:7:5:2 and suffix at 5:7:5:3, under the imperative at 5:7:1:2 and suffix at 5:7:1:3. Contact: the conjunction keeps the two accusative objects side by side under one verb. Result: favor and covenant are paired while remaining distinct things to remember.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold gratitude and obligation together without treating them as one undifferentiated idea.
findings.containment: The coordination preserves two objects; it does not assign them identical meaning or a fixed hierarchy beyond their local order.

epistemic.reason: Trusted local evidence directly supports the second-object coordination.

findings.title: The possessed covenant has binding force
findings.claim: مِيثَاقَهُ names a singular divine covenant as a firm binding instrument and second object of recall.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the covenant noun at 5:7:5:2 and 3MS suffix at 5:7:5:3. Trigger: the recall imperative at 5:7:1:2 and suffix at 5:7:1:3, followed by the relative clause. Contact: possession and accusative coordination make this particular covenant the object that must be remembered. Result: the remembered promise carries firmness and binding force.
findings.reader_payoff: The covenant becomes a concrete bond held under a named owner, rather than a loose promise.
findings.containment: The claim stays with the supplied possessed noun and local binding pressure; it does not reconstruct a whole covenant history.

epistemic.reason: Trusted word-analysis evidence supports the singular possessed covenant and its object role.

findings.title: The following clause defines the covenant
findings.claim: ٱلَّذِى locks the following binding clause onto the covenant rather than onto the favor.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the masculine singular relative pronoun at 5:7:6:1. Trigger: its antecedent covenant noun at 5:7:5:2 and suffix at 5:7:5:3, followed by the verb at 5:7:7:1 and suffix at 5:7:7:2. Contact: agreement directs the relative clause back to the covenant. Result: the covenant is specified through the enacted binding that follows.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the noun remain open for a moment, then become defined by what was done with it.
findings.containment: The antecedent relation is local and grammatical; it does not exclude the favor from the broader command, only from this relative-clause attachment.

epistemic.reason: Trusted local evidence supports the relative pronoun's agreement and antecedent.

findings.title: The covenant is enacted relationally
findings.claim: وَاثَقَكُمْ describes a completed relational covenanting act that includes the addressees within the binding frame.
findings.mechanism: Carrier: the completed Form III verb at 5:7:7:1 and 2MP object at 5:7:7:2. Trigger: the covenant instrument at 5:7:5:2 and suffix at 5:7:5:3, with the relative clause at 5:7:6:1. Contact: the relational form joins the named bond to the addressed community as participants in the act. Result: the covenant is presented as enacted binding, with reciprocity bounded by the divine-human frame.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the covenant as an action involving the addressed community, not only as an object stored in memory.
findings.containment: The relational force is limited to covenantal participation in this form; it does not assert unlimited equivalence between the parties.

epistemic.reason: Trusted evidence supports the rare Form III relation, while the finding explicitly bounds the reciprocity claim.

findings.title: Recollection becomes voiced renewal
findings.claim: The remembrance command can be read as re-presenting the favor through voiced renewal of the confirmed bond and its response.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is the remembrance form at 5:7:1:2, with the covenant forms at 5:7:5:2 and 5:7:7:1 and the speech form at 5:7:10:1 as independent contacts. The HFT trace joins mental recall to spoken mention, confirmed covenant, and quoted response. Their contact changes private recollection into an attributed image of publicly voiced covenant renewal.
findings.reader_payoff: The remembered favor can be perceived as returning into active presence through the words that voiced and renewed the bond.
findings.containment: This is an attributed reconstructed HFT reading with legacy_unbound provenance; it deepens the ordinary recall command without claiming that all remembrance is public speech or that the external docket is adjudicated.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus-local trace is coordinate-complete and returns through supplied focus words, but its reader identity is legacy_unbound and its branch roles remain attributed.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Unutulmuş veya gözden uzaklaşmış bir bilgiyi yeniden bilince getirme eylemidir.
branch_activations.carrier: The remembrance imperative carries mental recovery of what has receded from awareness.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The named favor and the later quoted response give the command a concrete event to bring back.
branch_activations.activation: The recollection carrier meets the favor object and voiced covenant response, so remembrance becomes re-presencing of the covenant scene.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The commanded remembrance can re-present the favor together with the confirmed spoken bond and its response.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not make every act of speech a remembrance or claim a general public-memory theory.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir kişi, nesne veya konuyu dilde söz olarak geçirmek ve adını söylemektir.
branch_activations.carrier: The remembrance form carries the possibility of articulated mention in this commanded scene.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: قُلْتُمْ supplies an explicit spoken utterance as a separate focus word.
branch_activations.activation: The spoken response meets the remembrance carrier, allowing the act of remembering to include verbal mention here.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The covenant is remembered through an articulated declaration as well as mental recovery.
branch_activations.boundary: The attributed reading concerns this covenant quotation; it does not activate every speech-related use of remembrance.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Tarafları bağlayan ve tutulması güçlü biçimde güvence altına alınmış söz veya anlaşma.
branch_activations.carrier: The covenant noun and relational covenanting verb carry a confirmed binding agreement.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The quoted response makes the bond a declared and remembered commitment.
branch_activations.activation: The binding covenant meets the voiced response, giving the remembered favor a concrete covenant object.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Remembrance re-presents a confirmed bond rather than an undefined old promise.
branch_activations.boundary: The reading concerns the supplied covenant frame and does not claim a complete legal account of the bond.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Çekirdek işlem, sözü sesli olarak dışa çıkarmaktır.
branch_activations.carrier: The completed speech verb carries the outward voicing of the addressees' words.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The paired hearing-and-obedience formula supplies the covenant response being voiced.
branch_activations.activation: The speech carrier meets the two response verbs, turning assent into an audible articulated declaration.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The remembered covenant includes the sound of the community declaring its response.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not claim that every utterance is covenantal or that outward voicing alone guarantees inward agreement.

findings.title: The response forms a trust-to-action circuit
findings.claim: The covenant, hearing, obedience, and self-guarding can be read as a continuing trust-to-action circuit that the final command preserves.
findings.mechanism: The carriers are the covenant forms at 5:7:5:2 and 5:7:7:1, hearing at 5:7:11:1, obedience at 5:7:12:2, and guarding at 5:7:13:2. The HFT trace makes the covenant relational ground, hearing receptive understanding, obedience willing alignment, and taqwa the protective continuation. Their contact changes the quoted response from a completed report into an attributed circuit carried into present conduct.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive hearing and obedience as connected stages whose trust must remain protected in conduct.
findings.containment: This is an attributed reconstructed HFT reading with legacy_unbound provenance; it supports the ordinary sequence without claiming that the response is the only possible framing or that taqwa is reducible to the circuit.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus-local trace supplies matching response coordinates and returns through focus words, but its reader identity is legacy_unbound and its branch roles are attributed.

findings.title: The closing clause audits the pledge's inner source
findings.claim: The spoken pledge can be read alongside the final interior domain as an attributed audit of whether outward assent and its inward source agree.
findings.mechanism: The carriers are the speech form at 5:7:10:1, the knowing predicate at 5:7:17:1, and the chest domain at 5:7:19:2. The HFT trace uses the interior-speech facet of saying, knowledge of what is true, and the source from which conduct issues. Their contact moves the audit behind the audible formula to the interior source generating speech and action.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the final knowledge assertion reaching behind the public words to the interior from which conduct arises.
findings.containment: This is an attributed reconstructed HFT reading with legacy_unbound provenance; it adds an inward accountability pressure while preserving the ordinary claim that God knows what is in the chests.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus-local trace supplies matching speech, knowledge, and interior coordinates, but its reader identity is legacy_unbound and its branch roles are attributed.
